page: Microsoft Azure DC64es_v6 is a general-purpose confidential computing virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon processors featuring Intel Trust Domain Extensions (TDX), the instance provides 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 256 GB, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU allocation alongside a sizable 260 MB L3 cache. Architectural acceleration includes AVX-512, Intel AMX tile and int8 matrix instructions, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The server does not include bundled local disk storage or discrete GPUs, relying on remote premium storage attachments for stateful filesystems. In CPU benchmarks, the DC64es_v6 yields average results, recording 1907.78 in stress-ng single-core and 60577.88 in multi-core execution. Conversely, memory subsystem responsiveness is competitive, demonstrated by 77.0 million operations per second in redis SET tests, placing it in the top quartile. The absence of local disk drives trade-offs in raw storage latency, but the hardware configuration delivers balanced resource scaling for confidential computing, in-memory caching tiers, microservices, and enterprise application backends.

The configuration supplies 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 256 GB of system RAM (4.0 GB per vCPU), and a substantial 260 MB L3 cache, with support for advanced matrix extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instructions. The server contains no local storage or GPUs, utilizing external premium storage for persistence. In synthetic evaluations, the instance yields average multi-core and single-core stress-ng throughput while delivering strong in-memory performance, achieving 77.0 million operations per second in redis SET operations. Without local storage overhead, the DC64es_v6 represents a balanced resource allocation for memory-resident databases, secure enterprise applications, confidential data processing, and general-purpose workloads.
